Thanks for the call earlier, Marissa — good overview. A few follow-ups from our side to help decide between Dedicated vs Private: 

1) SSO: we use Okta SAML and need IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. We also require JIT provisioning for service accounts. Will a Dedicated environment support our SAML metadata + SCIM provisioning, or is that only available in Private?

2) KMS/HSM: compliance wants customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys for all production encryption at rest for models and logs. Does Redwood Dedicated allow BYOK with AWS KMS or external HSM, or do we need Private for full HSM control?

3) Logging and retention: auditor wants 365 days of request/response logging and immutable export to our S3. We heard hosted has 90-day retention and Dedicated has configurable retention — need to confirm exact guarantees and export paths.

4) Network: for the private data flows, we prefer VPC peering or private link. Is that available on Dedicated or only Private?

Can you confirm which requirements force us to Private vs which can be satisfied in Dedicated? Also please attach any sample architecture docs and a ballpark cost delta.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex — great questions, thanks for laying them out. Below is a short recap and where things typically land. I've looped in Dylan (SE) and Rachel (Solutions) to confirm technical details and next steps.

Quick answers up front:
- SSO (SAML + SCIM): Supported on Dedicated (Okta SAML/SP-initiated + SCIM v2 provisioning). Private gives the same plus additional network-level IdP integrations for on-prem IdPs.
- KMS/HSM (BYOK): Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (BYOK). Full external HSM integrations (on-prem HSM appliances or HSM-as-a-service with private network bindings) currently require Private.
- Logging & retention: Dedicated can be configured to retain logs longer than the hosted default and supports streaming to your S3 (we typically support configurable retention up to 2 years; immutable export requires Private or a signed write-to-S3 pipeline we can enable).
- Network (VPC peering / PrivateLink): VPC peering and PrivateLink are available on Private. Dedicated supports private connectivity options (customer VLAN or VPN) but the tightest network isolation (no internet egress) is Private.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dylan: can you confirm the BYOK flow we'd present for Dedicated (AWS KMS steps + any limitations) and what HSM features require Private?
2) Rachel: can you attach the deployment options PDF and a ballpark monthly delta for Dedicated vs Private for their projected throughput?
3) Alex / Sanjay: please send your Okta metadata and a short list of compliance artifacts you need (e.g., HSM certs, specific SOC2 controls). I attached our high-level options doc to this thread.

I'll also prepare an internal note mapping each FintechCo requirement to Dedicated vs Private to make the decision easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical clarifications from the SE side: 

SSO/SCIM
- Dedicated: supports SAML 2.0 (IdP/SP) with both SP- and IdP-initiated flows. SCIM v2 provisioning works via a service account with scoped permissions. We recommend Okta service account provisioning for automated user lifecycle.

KMS/BYOK
- Dedicated: supports AWS KMS customer-managed CMKs. You provide the key ARN and grant Redwood's KMS principal access; keys reside in your AWS account. This satisfies most PCI/PII controls.
- Private: required if you need on-prem HSM appliances, HSM-tier key material that never leaves your HSM, or FIPS 140-2/3 specific HSM integrations where the KMS provider is not acceptable. Private also supports HSM-as-a-service via private connectivity in some regions.

Logging/Retention
- Dedicated: we can stream request/response logs to your S3 bucket via a secure write role; retention is configurable up to 2 years. For immutable, tamper-evident archives we recommend configuring S3 Object Lock + Glacier for long-term retention (we can provide IaC templates).
- Private: you can keep logs fully inside your network and use your existing retention/compliance tooling.

Network
- Dedicated supports VPN and private VLANs; egress still routes through our dedicated fabric. If you need zero public egress and full network isolation, choose Private (VPC peering + full control plane in your VPC).

Known limitations to call out:
- Dedicated BYOK with AWS KMS: keys must be in a supported cloud region and we currently support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault for CMKs. External HSM appliance integrations (FIPS HSM in your DC) require Private.
- SCIM: enterprise provisioning rate limits apply — for very large orgs (>100k users) we recommend an initial provisioning sync approach.

I'll draft a short tech note mapping your three asks to the two deployment modes and attach it. Happy to do a follow-up technical call with your infra team.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
